methods.label: Track the tripling dates
methods.explanation:
For the intended estimate, assume growth is spread reasonably steadily between the \(25\)-year checkpoints. Starting with \(200\) people in \(1998\), successive checkpoints give \(600\) in \(2023\), \(1800\) in \(2048\), and
\[
1800\times3=5400
\]
in \(2073\). The next checkpoint has \(16{,}200\) people, so \(6000\) is near the \(2073\) checkpoint. The closest offered year to \(2073\) is \(2075\), giving the intended choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

Without a rule for growth between checkpoints, the choice is not forced. Suppose instead that the population stays constant except for tripling jumps in \(1999,2024,2049,2074,\ldots\). The jumps are \(25\) years apart, and the populations at the original checkpoints still triple. Yet this schedule has \(5400\) people in \(2050\) and \(16{,}200\) in \(2075\), so choice A would better approximate when the population is \(6000\). Thus B depends on the intended within-period interpretation.
